symbols.name: big-O bound
symbols.meaning: The asymptotic upper bound notation: a function is O(g) when it is at most a constant times g for all large inputs.
symbols.quote: Here $O(g)$ means at most a constant times $g$ for all large inputs.

symbols.name: binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1, so that lg n = max{ceil(log2 n), 1}.
symbols.quote: $\lg n = \max\{\lceil \log_2 n\rceil, 1\}$ is the base-2 logarithm rounded up and at least 1.

relations.quote: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time disproves the [Schönhage–Strassen n log n conjecture](nlogn-conjecture.md) in this model.
It computes its polynomial products by the [Harvey–van der Hoeven O(n log n) multiplication](harvey-hoeven-multiplier.md) on packed integers from [Signed Kronecker packing](kronecker-packing.md).
The power saving follows from [Recursive power saving](recursive-power-saving.md).
The integer product is reduced to a convolution of radix-$2^b$ digit sequences, with carries restored to binary, as in [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md).
The algorithm arranges its digits by the [Chinese-remainder address map](chinese-remainder-address-map.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes.
It computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which expresses each prime-length transform through power-of-two axes.
It converts its middle transform by [Bluestein's chirp identity](bluestein-chirp.md) into a normalized cyclic convolution.

relations.predicate: places its last cyclic coordinate in
relations.quote: It places its last cyclic coordinate in the [Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md), where its wrap is a signed shift.
It computes its forward transforms by [Synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md), which keep frequency order through their pointwise product.

The algorithm builds each transform level from a [Simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-butterfly-layer.md), which acts on one address bit of every record, and whose cost is $O(V d^{\lambda'})$ for $\lambda'<1$.
The algorithm performs its address permutations by [Fast address interchange](address-interchange.md), whose cost is $O(V u^\tau)$ for $\tau<1$.
The algorithm recovers its exact product by [Exact recovery by rounding](rounding-recovery.md), which rounds the approximate coefficients to integers and propagates carries.
